title: Model Compression & Pruning
description: Model compression: Büyük modelleri küçültme (size ↓, speed ↑, accuracy ~). Pruning (weights remove), quantization (precision ↓), knowledge distillation (teacher→student). Mobile, edge, production deployment.

content.level0_basic: Model Compression, büyük modelleri küçültme işlemidir. Amaç: Model size ↓ (100MB → 10MB), inference speed ↑ (10ms → 2ms), accuracy ~ (minimal loss). Teknikler: (1) **Pruning**: Gereksiz weights/neurons remove (sparse matrix). (2) **Quantization**: FP32 → INT8 (4x smaller, 2-4x faster). (3) **Knowledge Distillation**: Büyük teacher model → küçük student model. (4) **Low-Rank Factorization**: Matrix decomposition (W = UV). Kullanım: Mobile (iOS, Android), edge devices (IoT, Raspberry Pi), production (latency critical).
content.level1_beginner: Compression teknikleri detay: (1) **Pruning**: (a) Weight pruning: Küçük weights'i sıfırla (|w|<threshold). (b) Neuron pruning: Tüm neuron'u remove. (c) Structured pruning: Channel/filter pruning (CNN). Unstructured (sparse, 50-90% sparsity) vs structured (dense, 30-50% faster). (2) **Quantization**: (a) Post-training quantization (PTQ): Train sonrası convert (FP32→INT8). (b) Quantization-aware training (QAT): Train sırasında quantization simulate. INT8: 4x smaller, 2-4x faster, <1% accuracy loss. (3) **Knowledge Distillation**: Teacher (büyük, accurate) → Student (küçük, fast). Loss = student_loss + α·distillation_loss (soft labels). (4) **Architecture Search**: MobileNet, EfficientNet (compact design). Metrikler: Model size (MB), FLOPs, inference time (ms), accuracy drop (%).
content.level2_application: Pratik uygulamalar: (1) **Mobile ML**: iOS CoreML, Android TFLite. MobileNet, EfficientNet. Quantization (INT8), pruning (50% sparsity). Real-time (<100ms). (2) **Edge Devices**: IoT, Raspberry Pi. TinyML. Extreme compression (1-10MB models). INT8/INT4 quantization. (3) **Production Serving**: Latency critical (search, recommendation). Model size ↓ → memory usage ↓ → more models per server. Batch processing faster. (4) **NLP**: BERT (340MB) → DistilBERT (207MB), TinyBERT (57MB), ALBERT (12MB). Quantization + distillation. 2-5x faster, <3% accuracy loss. (5) **Computer Vision**: ResNet-50 (98MB) → MobileNetV3 (20MB), EfficientNet-B0 (29MB). Pruning + quantization. Real-time video. (6) **Voice Assistants**: On-device wake word detection. Tiny models (<1MB). Low power. Framework'ler: TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime, PyTorch Mobile, TensorRT (NVIDIA).

(1) **Production Pipeline**: Train (FP32) → Prune (50-90% sparsity) → Finetune → Quantize (INT8/INT4) → Calibrate → Validate (accuracy drop <1-3%) → Deploy (TFLite/ONNX/TensorRT) → Monitor (latency, throughput, accuracy). (5) **Dynamic Models**: Dynamic depth (early exit), dynamic width (adaptive channels). Conditional computation (MoE). (6) **Fairness & Robustness**: Compression'ın bias'a etkisi. Protected groups'ta accuracy drop? Adversarial robustness (pruned models more vulnerable?). (7) **Federated Compression**: Edge devices'ta compression (communication cost ↓). On-device training + compression. Research: **Lottery Ticket Hypothesis** (winning tickets), **Zero-cost NAS** (no training), **Gradient-free optimization**, **Neural ODE compression**.

whatIsIt: Model Compression: Model size/complexity azaltma, accuracy preserve. Matematiksel: Sparse model: ||W||_0 << parameters (L0 norm). Quantization: W ∈ {-127,...,127} (INT8), 256 values. Knowledge Distillation: L = L_CE(y, ŷ_student) + α·L_KL(ŷ_teacher, ŷ_student). Low-Rank: W ≈ U·V^T, rank(W) = k << min(m,n). Metrikler: Compression ratio (original/compressed), FLOPs reduction (%), inference speedup (x), accuracy drop (%).
whyNeeded: Model compression kritik çünkü: (1) **Mobile Deployment**: Smartphones memory limited (100MB-1GB models too big). App size limit (iOS 150MB). Battery (inference energy). (2) **Edge Devices**: IoT, cameras, drones. Memory <512MB, compute limited. Real-time (<100ms). (3) **Latency Critical**: Search (50ms SLA), recommendation (10ms), autonomous driving (<10ms). Smaller model → faster inference. (4) **Cost**: Cloud inference cost ∝ model size. 10x smaller → 10x cheaper. More models per server (GPU memory). (5) **Privacy**: On-device inference (no data sent to cloud). Medical, financial data. (6) **Energy**: Data centers (training+inference) carbon footprint. Smaller models → less energy. Green AI. (7) **Democratization**: Large models (GPT-4, 1.7T params) inaccessible. Compressed models (distillation) → everyone can use.
realWorldAnalogy: Model compression'ı seyahat bagajına benzetebiliriz. **Durum**: 100kg eşya (büyük model), uçak bagaj limit 20kg (mobile device memory). **Hedef**: 20kg'a indir, önemli şeyleri koru. **Teknikler**: (1) **Pruning (Çıkar)**: Gereksiz eşyaları at (nadir kullanılan, duplicate). Weight magnitude: Rarely used items → remove. 50-90% eşya gider ama functionality ~. (2) **Quantization (Sıkıştır)**: Vacuum bag (havayı çıkar). FP32 → INT8: Her item'ı 4x küçült (detay kaybı minimal). Şişman sweater → compressed. (3) **Knowledge Distillation (Öğret)**: Büyük valize (teacher) bak, küçük valize (student) önemli bilgiyi aktar. Student teacher'ı taklit eder, %90-95 functionality. (4) **Low-Rank (Reorganize)**: Matrix decomposition. Eşyaları smart organize et (overlap, efficient packing). **Trade-off**: Çok aggressive compression → önemli eşya kaybolur (accuracy drop). Balance: Size ↓, utility ~.

formulas: \text{Low-Rank Factorization}: \quad W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n} \approx U \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times k} \cdot V^T \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}, \quad k \ll \min(m,n)

stepByStep: 1. **Baseline**: Original model train et (FP32, full size). Baseline metrics: Model size (MB), FLOPs, inference time (ms), accuracy (%). Hardware target: Mobile (iOS/Android), Edge (Raspberry Pi), Cloud (GPU/CPU).

2. **Compression Strategy**: (a) Latency critical + mobile → Quantization (INT8) + structured pruning. (b) Memory critical + edge → Aggressive pruning (90% sparsity) + quantization (INT4). (c) Accuracy critical + cloud → Knowledge distillation + mild pruning. (d) Extreme → TinyML (binary/ternary networks, <1MB).

3. **Pruning**: (a) Magnitude-based: Compute |W|, sort, prune bottom 50-90%. (b) Structured: Remove entire channels/filters (CNN), neurons (FC). (c) Iterative: Prune 10-20%, finetune, repeat. (d) Sensitivity analysis: Per-layer sparsity (critical layers less pruning). (e) Finetune: 5-10 epochs, lower LR.

4. **Knowledge Distillation**: (a) Train teacher (large, accurate). (b) Teacher inference (soft labels, temperature T=3-5). (c) Train student (small), loss = CE(y, ŷ_student) + α·KL(teacher, student), α=0.5-0.9. (d) Student mimics teacher distribution. (e) Validate: Accuracy drop <3%.

5. **Quantization**: (a) Post-Training Quantization (PTQ): Model trained (FP32), convert to INT8 (calibration dataset 100-1000 samples). Fast, <1% accuracy loss (typical). (b) Quantization-Aware Training (QAT): Simulate quantization during training (fake quantization). Better accuracy (<0.5% loss), longer training. (c) Dynamic vs Static: Dynamic (runtime), Static (calibration, faster).

6. **Hybrid**: Pruning + Quantization + Distillation. (a) Distill (teacher→student), (b) Prune student (50-70%), (c) Finetune, (d) Quantize (INT8), (e) Validate. Stacking techniques → higher compression (10-20x).

7. **Validation**: Test set evaluation (original distribution). Metrikler: (a) Model size (MB, compression ratio). (b) FLOPs (compute reduction). (c) Inference time (ms, speedup). (d) Accuracy (drop <1-3%). (e) Per-class accuracy (fairness). Hardware: Actual device (mobile/edge), not only simulation.

8. **Conversion**: Export compressed model. (a) TensorFlow → TFLite (mobile), TF-TRT (NVIDIA). (b) PyTorch → ONNX → ONNX Runtime (cross-platform). (c) TensorRT (NVIDIA GPU, high performance). (d) CoreML (iOS), NNAPI (Android). Operator support check (some ops not supported).

9. **Optimization**: Hardware-specific. (a) Operator fusion (conv+BN+ReLU → single op). (b) Memory layout (NCHW vs NHWC). (c) Multi-threading (CPU). (d) GPU/NPU acceleration. (e) Batch size tuning (latency vs throughput). Profiling: TensorFlow Profiler, PyTorch Profiler.

10. **Production Deployment**: (a) A/B test (compressed vs original). (b) Monitor: Latency (p50, p99), throughput (QPS), accuracy (online metrics). (c) Rollback plan (if accuracy drops). (d) Gradual rollout (1% → 10% → 100%). (e) Retraining: New data → retrain compressed model.
algorithm.complexity: **Model Size**: Pruning: s·params (sparsity s=0.5-0.9), Quantization: 4-8x smaller (FP32→INT8), Distillation: student params (e.g., 0.5x teacher), Combined: 10-100x. **Inference Time**: Pruning: Unstructured (sparse, 1.5-2x speedup with sparse kernels), Structured (dense, 2-3x speedup), Quantization: 2-4x speedup (INT8 vs FP32), Distillation: depends on student size, Combined: 5-10x speedup. **Training Time**: Pruning: +10-20% (iterative finetune), Distillation: +50-100% (teacher inference + student training), QAT: +20-50% (fake quantization overhead). **Uzay**: Pruning: Sparse storage (COO, CSR formats), Quantization: 4x less memory, Low-Rank: k·(m+n) vs m·n. **Hardware**: Sparse: NVIDIA Ampere (sparse tensor cores), INT8: Most modern CPUs/GPUs, TensorRT: NVIDIA GPU optimization.

codeExamples.title: Magnitude-Based Pruning (PyTorch)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.utils.prune as prune
import copy

# Simple model
class SimpleNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(784, 256)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(256, 128)
        self.fc3 = nn.Linear(128, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = torch.relu(self.fc2(x))
        return self.fc3(x)

model = SimpleNet()

# Count parameters
def count_parameters(model):
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())

def count_nonzero(model):
    return sum((p != 0).sum().item() for p in model.parameters())

print(f'Original parameters: {count_parameters(model):,}')
print(f'Non-zero: {count_nonzero(model):,}')

# Magnitude-based pruning (50% sparsity)
for name, module in model.named_modules():
    if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
        prune.l1_unstructured(module, name='weight', amount=0.5)
        prune.remove(module, 'weight')  # Make pruning permanent

sparsity = 1 - count_nonzero(model) / count_parameters(model)
print(f'\nAfter 50% pruning:')
print(f'Non-zero: {count_nonzero(model):,}')
print(f'Sparsity: {sparsity*100:.1f}%')
print(f'Compression ratio: {1/(1-sparsity):.1f}x')

print('\nNote: Unstructured pruning requires sparse kernels for speedup.')
codeExamples.explanation: Magnitude pruning: Küçük weights'i (|w|<threshold) sıfırla. 50% sparsity → 2x compression (with sparse storage). Finetune gerekir.

codeExamples.title: Post-Training Quantization (TensorFlow)
codeExamples.code:
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np
import os

# Create simple model
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(128, activation='relu', input_shape=(784,)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])

model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])

# Dummy training (replace with real data)
X_train = np.random.randn(1000, 784).astype('float32')
y_train = np.random.randint(0, 10, 1000)
model.fit(X_train, y_train, epochs=5, verbose=0)

print('Original model:')
print(f'Size: {os.path.getsize("temp_model.h5")/1e6:.2f} MB' if os.path.exists('temp_model.h5') else 'Not saved yet')

# Save original
model.save('temp_model.h5')
original_size = os.path.getsize('temp_model.h5')
print(f'Original size: {original_size/1e6:.2f} MB')

# Post-Training Quantization
converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_keras_model(model)
converter.optimizations = [tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT]  # Quantize to INT8

# Representative dataset for calibration
def representative_dataset():
    for i in range(100):
        yield [X_train[i:i+1]]

converter.representative_dataset = representative_dataset
converter.target_spec.supported_ops = [tf.lite.OpsSet.TFLITE_BUILTINS_INT8]
converter.inference_input_type = tf.int8
converter.inference_output_type = tf.int8

tflite_model = converter.convert()

# Save quantized
with open('quantized_model.tflite', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(tflite_model)

quantized_size = os.path.getsize('quantized_model.tflite')
print(f'\nQuantized size: {quantized_size/1e6:.2f} MB')
print(f'Compression ratio: {original_size/quantized_size:.1f}x')
print(f'Reduction: {(1 - quantized_size/original_size)*100:.1f}%')

print('\nQuantization: FP32 → INT8 (4x smaller, 2-4x faster)')

# Cleanup
os.remove('temp_model.h5')
os.remove('quantized_model.tflite')
codeExamples.explanation: Post-Training Quantization: FP32→INT8. 4x smaller, 2-4x faster inference. <1% accuracy loss (typical). TFLite for mobile.

codeExamples.title: Knowledge Distillation (PyTorch)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import numpy as np

# Teacher: Large model
class TeacherNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(784, 512)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(512, 256)
        self.fc3 = nn.Linear(256, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = F.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = F.relu(self.fc2(x))
        return self.fc3(x)

# Student: Small model
class StudentNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(784, 64)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(64, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = F.relu(self.fc1(x))
        return self.fc2(x)

# Distillation loss
def distillation_loss(student_logits, teacher_logits, labels, T=3, alpha=0.7):
    # Soft targets (teacher)
    soft_loss = F.kl_div(
        F.log_softmax(student_logits / T, dim=1),
        F.softmax(teacher_logits / T, dim=1),
        reduction='batchmean'
    ) * (T * T)
    
    # Hard targets (labels)
    hard_loss = F.cross_entropy(student_logits, labels)
    
    return alpha * soft_loss + (1 - alpha) * hard_loss

# Models
teacher = TeacherNet()
student = StudentNet()

print(f'Teacher params: {sum(p.numel() for p in teacher.parameters()):,}')
print(f'Student params: {sum(p.numel() for p in student.parameters()):,}')
print(f'Compression: {sum(p.numel() for p in teacher.parameters())/sum(p.numel() for p in student.parameters()):.1f}x smaller')

# Dummy data
X = torch.randn(100, 784)
y = torch.randint(0, 10, (100,))

# Assume teacher is trained
teacher.eval()

# Train student
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(student.parameters(), lr=0.001)

print('\nTraining student with distillation...')
for epoch in range(50):
    student.train()
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    
    student_logits = student(X)
    with torch.no_grad():
        teacher_logits = teacher(X)
    
    loss = distillation_loss(student_logits, teacher_logits, y, T=3, alpha=0.7)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    
    if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
        print(f'Epoch {epoch+1}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')

print('\nDistillation: Student mimics teacher (soft labels). Smaller model, ~accuracy.')
codeExamples.explanation: Knowledge Distillation: Teacher (big, accurate) → Student (small, fast). Soft labels (temperature T). Loss = hard + α·soft. Student 5-10x smaller, <3% accuracy drop.

codeExamples.title: Structured Pruning (Channel Pruning)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

# Conv model
class ConvNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, channels1=64, channels2=128):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, channels1, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(channels1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(channels1, channels2, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(channels2)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(channels2 * 8 * 8, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = F.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
        x = F.max_pool2d(x, 2)
        x = F.relu(self.bn2(self.conv2(x)))
        x = F.max_pool2d(x, 2)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        return self.fc(x)

# Original
model_original = ConvNet(channels1=64, channels2=128)
print('Original model:')
print(f'Conv1: 64 channels, Conv2: 128 channels')
print(f'Parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model_original.parameters()):,}')

# Pruned: 50% channels
model_pruned = ConvNet(channels1=32, channels2=64)
print('\nPruned model (50% channels):')
print(f'Conv1: 32 channels, Conv2: 64 channels')
print(f'Parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model_pruned.parameters()):,}')

compression = sum(p.numel() for p in model_original.parameters()) / sum(p.numel() for p in model_pruned.parameters())
print(f'\nCompression ratio: {compression:.1f}x')

# Dummy inference time
import time
X = torch.randn(1, 3, 32, 32)

model_original.eval()
start = time.time()
for _ in range(100):
    _ = model_original(X)
original_time = (time.time() - start) / 100

model_pruned.eval()
start = time.time()
for _ in range(100):
    _ = model_pruned(X)
pruned_time = (time.time() - start) / 100

print(f'\nInference time:')
print(f'Original: {original_time*1000:.2f} ms')
print(f'Pruned: {pruned_time*1000:.2f} ms')
print(f'Speedup: {original_time/pruned_time:.1f}x')

print('\nStructured pruning: Remove entire channels/filters. Dense (hardware-friendly), 2-3x speedup.')
codeExamples.explanation: Structured Pruning: Tüm channel/filter remove. Dense matrix, hardware-friendly. 2-3x speedup, 30-50% smaller. Unstructured'dan daha practical.

codeExamples.title: Quantization-Aware Training (QAT)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.quantization as quantization

# Model
class SimpleNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.quant = quantization.QuantStub()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(784, 128)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, 10)
        self.dequant = quantization.DeQuantStub()
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.quant(x)
        x = self.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = self.fc2(x)
        x = self.dequant(x)
        return x

model = SimpleNet()
model.train()

print('Original model (FP32):')
print(f'Parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}')

# QAT: Prepare
model.qconfig = quantization.get_default_qat_qconfig('fbgemm')
quantization.prepare_qat(model, inplace=True)

print('\nQAT prepared (fake quantization):')
print('Training simulates INT8 quantization...')

# Dummy training
X = torch.randn(100, 784)
y = torch.randint(0, 10, (100,))
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

for epoch in range(10):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    outputs = model(X)
    loss = criterion(outputs, y)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    
    if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0:
        print(f'Epoch {epoch+1}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')

# Convert to quantized
model.eval()
quantization.convert(model, inplace=True)

print('\nConverted to INT8:')
print('Model now uses INT8 for inference.')
print('Benefits: 4x smaller, 2-4x faster, <0.5% accuracy loss')
print('\nQAT vs PTQ: QAT better accuracy (trains with quantization), PTQ easier.')
codeExamples.explanation: Quantization-Aware Training: Train sırasında quantization simulate (fake quant). Better accuracy (<0.5% drop) vs PTQ. FP32→INT8, 4x smaller, 2-4x faster.

codeExamples.title: Model Size & FLOPs Analysis
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torchsummary import summary  # pip install torchsummary
import numpy as np

# Model
class CNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(128 * 8 * 8, 256)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(256, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = torch.relu(self.conv1(x))
        x = torch.max_pool2d(x, 2)
        x = torch.relu(self.conv2(x))
        x = torch.max_pool2d(x, 2)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        return self.fc2(x)

model = CNN()

# Model size
print('=== Model Analysis ===')
print(f'\nParameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}')

# Size in MB (FP32)
size_fp32 = sum(p.numel() * 4 for p in model.parameters()) / 1e6  # 4 bytes per FP32
size_int8 = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) / 1e6  # 1 byte per INT8

print(f'\nModel Size:')
print(f'FP32: {size_fp32:.2f} MB')
print(f'INT8 (quantized): {size_int8:.2f} MB ({size_fp32/size_int8:.1f}x smaller)')

# FLOPs (approximate)
def count_flops(model, input_size=(1, 3, 32, 32)):
    total_flops = 0
    x = torch.randn(*input_size)
    
    # Conv1: (C_out * C_in * K * K * H_out * W_out)
    # FC: (in_features * out_features)
    
    # Simplified (actual FLOPs higher with activations, etc.)
    for module in model.modules():
        if isinstance(module, nn.Conv2d):
            out_h = input_size[2] // 2  # Assuming pooling
            out_w = input_size[3] // 2
            flops = module.out_channels * module.in_channels * module.kernel_size[0] * module.kernel_size[1] * out_h * out_w
            total_flops += flops
        elif isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            flops = module.in_features * module.out_features
            total_flops += flops
    
    return total_flops

flops = count_flops(model)
print(f'\nFLOPs (approximate): {flops/1e6:.2f} M')

print('\nCompression impact:')
print('50% pruning → 2x smaller, 2x fewer FLOPs')
print('INT8 quantization → 4x smaller, 2-4x faster inference')
print('Combined (pruning + quantization) → 8x smaller, 4-8x faster')

quiz.question: Model compression'ın temel amaçları nelerdir?
options: Model size ↓, inference speed ↑, accuracy ~ (minimal loss). Mobile/edge deployment
quiz.explanation: Compression: Size ↓ (100MB→10MB), speed ↑ (10ms→2ms), accuracy ~ (<1-3% loss). Mobile, edge, production için kritik.

quiz.question: Pruning nedir?
quiz.explanation: Pruning: Küçük weights sıfırla (|w|<threshold). Unstructured (sparse, 50-90%), Structured (channels, 30-50%). Finetune gerekir.

quiz.question: Quantization nasıl çalışır?
options: Precision azaltma: FP32→INT8 (4x smaller, 2-4x faster). PTQ vs QAT
quiz.explanation: Quantization: FP32 (32-bit) → INT8 (8-bit). 4x smaller, 2-4x faster. <1% accuracy loss. PTQ (post-training), QAT (training-aware).

quiz.question: Knowledge Distillation prensibi?
options: Teacher (büyük) → Student (küçük). Soft labels (temperature). Student mimics teacher
quiz.explanation: Distillation: Teacher (accurate) → Student (compact). Loss = CE(hard) + α·KL(soft). Student 5-10x smaller, <3% accuracy drop.

quiz.question: Structured vs Unstructured pruning?
options: Structured: Entire channels/filters remove (dense, hardware-friendly, 2-3x speedup). Unstructured: Individual weights (sparse, 1.5-2x)
quiz.explanation: Structured: Channel/filter pruning (dense matrix, hardware-friendly). Unstructured: Weight pruning (sparse, sparse kernels gerekir). Structured more practical.

quiz.question: INT8 quantization'ın avantajları?
options: 4x smaller (vs FP32), 2-4x faster inference, <1% accuracy loss. Most modern hardware supports
quiz.explanation: INT8: 256 values (-128 to 127). 4x smaller, 2-4x faster (CPU/GPU accelerated). <1% accuracy loss (PTQ). <0.5% (QAT).

quiz.question: TinyML nedir?
options: Extreme compression (<1MB models). Binary/ternary networks, INT4. IoT, edge devices
quiz.explanation: TinyML: <1MB models. Extreme quantization (INT4/INT2, binary), aggressive pruning. IoT, Raspberry Pi, microcontrollers. Low power.

quiz.question: Production compression pipeline?
options: Train(FP32) → Prune → Finetune → Quantize → Validate → Deploy(TFLite/ONNX) → Monitor
quiz.explanation: Pipeline: (1) Train full model, (2) Prune (50-90%), (3) Finetune, (4) Quantize (INT8), (5) Validate (accuracy <1-3% drop), (6) Deploy (TFLite/ONNX/TensorRT), (7) Monitor.

flashcards.back: Model size/complexity azaltma, accuracy preserve. Techniques: Pruning, Quantization, Distillation, Low-Rank. Mobile, edge, production için.
Gereksiz weights/neurons remove. Magnitude-based (|w|<threshold). Unstructured (sparse 50-90%), Structured (channels 30-50%). Finetune gerekir.
Precision azaltma: FP32→INT8 (4x smaller, 2-4x faster). PTQ (post-training, easy), QAT (training-aware, better accuracy <0.5% drop).
Teacher (big) → Student (small). Soft labels (T=3-5). Loss = CE(hard) + α·KL(soft). Student 5-10x smaller, <3% accuracy drop.
Entire channel/filter remove. Dense matrix, hardware-friendly, 2-3x speedup. Less compression (30-50%) vs unstructured (50-90%).
PTQ: Post-training, FP32→INT8, calibration (100-1000 samples), <1% loss, fast. QAT: Training-aware, fake quantization, <0.5% loss, longer.
r = Size_original / Size_compressed. Pruning: 2x, Quantization: 4x, Distillation: 5-10x, Combined: 10-100x. Target: <3% accuracy drop.
Mobile ML framework (iOS, Android). Quantization, operator optimization, NNAPI/GPU delegate. PTQ, QAT support. <50MB models typical.
Computational cost azaltma. Pruning: 50% weights → 50% FLOPs. Structured: 50% channels → 75% FLOPs (quadratic). Latency ↓.
Matrix decomposition: W (m×n) ≈ U(m×k)·V(k×n), k<<min(m,n). Parameters: mn → k(m+n). SVD, Tucker decomposition.
Target hardware (CPU/GPU/NPU). Operator fusion, memory layout (NCHW vs NHWC), multi-threading, sparse kernels (NVIDIA Ampere).
Extreme compression (<1MB). Binary/ternary networks (1-bit), INT4/INT2. IoT, microcontrollers (Arduino, STM32). Low power (<1mW).

commonMistakes.why: 90% pruning → accuracy collapse. Model can't recover without finetuning. Weights removed, network capacity lost.
commonMistakes.fix: Iterative pruning: Prune 10-20%, finetune 5-10 epochs, repeat. Monitor accuracy. Per-layer sensitivity (critical layers less pruning). Gradual sparsity.

commonMistakes.why: PTQ requires calibration dataset (100-1000 samples). No calibration → poor range estimation → accuracy drop >5%.
commonMistakes.fix: Calibration: Representative dataset (similar to training distribution). Static quantization (calibration), not dynamic (runtime). QAT for <0.5% loss.

commonMistakes.mistake: Test on simulation, not actual device
commonMistakes.why: Simulation (laptop GPU) ≠ actual device (mobile CPU). Operator support, memory, latency different. False confidence.
commonMistakes.fix: Test on target hardware: iOS (CoreML), Android (TFLite), Edge (Raspberry Pi). Measure actual latency (ms), memory (MB), battery. Profile (TensorFlow Profiler).

commonMistakes.why: Compression (pruning, quantization) → accuracy drop. Distillation after → student learns from damaged teacher. Sub-optimal.
commonMistakes.fix: Correct order: (1) Distill (teacher → student), (2) Prune student, (3) Finetune, (4) Quantize, (5) Validate. Or: Prune teacher first, then distill.

commonMistakes.why: Unstructured (sparse) requires sparse kernels (limited support). CPU/GPU don't accelerate sparse. 50% sparsity → 1.5x speedup (not 2x).
commonMistakes.fix: Structured pruning (channels, filters) → dense matrix, hardware-friendly, 2-3x speedup. Or: Use sparse-aware hardware (NVIDIA Ampere sparse tensor cores).

commonMistakes.why: Compression can bias towards majority class. Rare classes (minority) accuracy drop >> average. Fairness issue.
commonMistakes.fix: Monitor per-class accuracy. Protected groups check. Balanced validation set. Distillation: Multi-task loss (per-class weights). Finetune on hard examples.

commonMistakes.mistake: Deploy compressed model without A/B test
commonMistakes.why: Offline accuracy (test set) ≠ online accuracy (production). User behavior, data drift. Rollback zor.
commonMistakes.fix: A/B test: Compressed vs original (1% → 10% → 100%). Monitor online metrics (CTR, conversion, latency). Gradual rollout, rollback plan.
